title: An async batch path on NATS JetStream
goal: Accept offline jobs (POST /v1/batches) into a durable queue and run them in the background at the lowest priority, so batch work only uses capacity interactive traffic leaves free. Delivery is at-least-once; workers are idempotent; usage goes to the same ledger; a full queue pushes back.

changes.note: JetStream work-queue stream with file storage, max_msgs + discard new (backpressure), 2-minute duplicate window; pull consumer with ack_wait and max_deliver.
POST /v1/batches with a required Idempotency-Key (one transaction); GET /v1/batches/:id.
Pull loop, heartbeats, defer on 429/503, retries with full-jitter backoff, terminal failure after 5 deliveries, sweeper for the dual-write gap.
Internal token + tenant id for worker-to-gateway calls (constant-time compare).
Batch requests: lowest priority, not charged to the interactive bucket, deterministic request id, ledger source batch.
batches (unique tenant + idempotency key) and batch_items.
nats (JetStream, volume, monitoring on 8222) and worker.

verify.label: Submit a batch
verify.cmd: curl -s localhost:8080/v1/batches -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-batch-1' -d '{"requests":[{"custom_id":"q1","body":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Capital of Italy?"}],"max_tokens":16}},{"custom_id":"q2","body":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"2+2?"}],"max_tokens":8}}]}'

verify.label: Submit it again (a client retry)
verify.expect: HTTP 200 {"id":"batch_..." (the same id),"status":"exists"}: nothing is enqueued twice.

verify.label: Poll the result
verify.expect: counts.done reaches 2; each item has status done, a response and token counts.

verify.label: Usage landed in the ledger as batch
verify.cmd: docker compose exec postgres psql -U app -d llm -c "SELECT request_id, source, completion_tokens FROM usage_ledger WHERE source = 'batch'"
verify.expect: Rows with request_id batch:<batchId>:q1 and :q2: deterministic ids, so a redelivered job reuses the same row.

verify.label: Queue depth
verify.expect: {"pending":0,"inProgress":0} when drained; the NATS monitoring endpoint shows stream BATCH.

verify.label: Batch yields to interactive traffic
verify.cmd: docker compose logs worker | grep batch_job_deferred | tail -3
verify.expect: While you flood interactive requests (stage 3's loop), jobs get 503 from admission (batch only queues in the first half) and the worker logs batch_job_deferred with a retry delay.

concepts.how: At-least-once with explicit acks and ack_wait; effectively-once through idempotent processing.
A work queue (each message to one worker, deleted on ack) rather than a replayable log.
Postgres commit then queue publish is a dual write; the sweeper patches the gap the outbox pattern closes.
Idempotency-Key on submit, msgID dedupe on publish, primary keys on results and ledger.
Exponential backoff with full jitter on worker retries; a retry cap (max_deliver).
Idempotent pipelines: rerunning a job must not change the result or the bill.
The batch tier fills the headroom you must keep for peaks, at the lowest priority.

checkpoints.text: A batch of two requests completed and both results are in GET /v1/batches/:id.
Resubmitting with the same Idempotency-Key returned the same batch id with status exists.
Batch usage rows have deterministic request ids (batch:<id>:<custom_id>).
I saw batch jobs deferred while interactive traffic filled the queues.
